Information since May points to continued labor‑market strength and moderate growth, with 12‑month inflation still below 2 percent. The FOMC raised the federal funds rate to 1–1¼ percent, kept policy accommodative, and signaled a gradual balance‑sheet normalization in 2017 if conditions evolve as anticipated.

April 2017 SLOOS insights temper the outlook at the margin: domestic banks largely left C&I standards little changed, but continued to tighten in riskier segments—most notably auto loans and parts of CRE—while easing somewhat for credit cards and remaining willing to extend consumer installment credit. Foreign banks reported wider loan‑rate spreads and greater use of rate floors. This mixed, slightly tighter credit backdrop suggests bank lending will not provide a strong tailwind, reinforcing the Committee’s gradualism and close monitoring of inflation.

Overall tone: cautiously positive on growth and employment, moderated by below‑target inflation and mildly tighter bank lending in certain categories.
